summary: Port reproduces the sweeping narrow rainbow band and its hue walk almost exactly, but runs the whole cycle ~25% fast and turns the signature pulse from a full-rig white-out into a dim doubled coloured flash.
observations: Rig: manifest grid 16x16 (256 px). Neither side exposes any controls (probe: 'no settable controls' on both). Both sides report wantsSensors:false. Both sides are seed-independent: seed 1 and seed 7 produce byte-identical meanBrightness series over 240 frames on both orig and port.

Quiet regime (most of the time) is a near-perfect match on both sides: a single narrow diagonal bright band, ~2-3 px FWHM, peaking at ~250/255, sliding across the grid while its angle slowly rotates, on a soft same-hue background gradient. --dump at t=5.5/5.6/5.7 s (row 8) gives orig 5,15,36,77,148,245,137,70,33,13,... and port 3,8,17,32,56,91,143,216,203,134,85,... — same Gaussian-ish profile, same peak amplitude.

Colour: both walk hue continuously and monotonically through the full wheel in the same direction. Orig completes one full 0->360 revolution in 6.55 s; port in 5.25 s (measured by hue of mean RGB at 20 and 40 fps; autocorrelation of meanBrightness gives 131 frames @20fps for orig and 105 frames @20fps for port, and the same seconds at 10/20/40 fps).

PULSE CADENCE: both sides fire a bright pulse each time the hue crosses 0 and 180. Orig: one pulse every 3.275 s (100 fps run, 12 s: peaks at 3.27 s, 6.54 s, 9.82 s). Port: pulses arrive as a PAIR every 2.62 s (pair centres 2.6 s, 5.23 s, 7.85 s, 10.47 s). Port's tempo is ~1.25x the original's.

PULSE AMPLITUDE: at its own peak the original whites out the ENTIRE rig — --dump at t=3.25 s: whole-grid mean 252, 256/256 px above 32, 225/256 px at >=250, mean(max channel) == mean(RGB) == 252, i.e. essentially all pixels (255,255,255). At t=6.525 s: mean 239, 256/256 lit. The port never gets close: its strongest peak in 40 s at 40 fps is whole-grid mean 85, and --dump at its own peak t=5.125 s gives mean 79 with mean(max channel) 141 and only 1/256 px saturated — a mid-brightness COLOURED wash, never a white-out.

PULSE SHAPE: orig fires one flash per pulse. At the hue-180 pulse it is a smooth symmetric bell ~1 s wide with no blackout (40 fps frames 113-145: 18,...,121,164,252,169,123,...,18). At the hue-0 pulse it is black (frames 253-257 = 0-2) then a single ~1-frame spike to 239 then black again (frames 267-269 = 0-1). Port instead fires TWO flashes ~0.2-0.3 s apart with a hard black notch between them: 40 fps frames 95-113 read 43,55,66,72,56,18,4,0,0,0,0,1,7,28,63,70,62,51,40 — flash, five black frames, second flash. Same at its hue-0 pulse (79 at f205, 0 at f208-210, 78 at f212).

Consequence in the stats: orig zeroMotionFrames 1/800 and 13 blackout stretches in 40 s at 20 fps, clustered as pairs around the hue-0 pulse only; port has ~30 blackout stretches, roughly one every 52 frames (2.6 s), i.e. the port goes fully dark about 2.5x as often as the original.
Both sides are frame-rate independent: the hue period measures 6.55 s (orig) / 5.25 s (port) identically at 10, 20 and 40 fps, so the tempo error is a real speed constant, not frame-rate coupling.

Resolution independence matches: re-rendered at --grid 48x48 both sides keep the same feature sizes and the same cadence (orig peaks at 3.25/6.50/9.80 s reaching 170-239; port pairs at 2.40/2.70, 5.10/5.30, 7.65/7.95, 10.35 s reaching 61-82). The divergences above are not a grid-size artefact.

Supplementary 3D lens (--rig cloud --pixels 1000, 12 s): both waterfalls show the same 3D character — a plane sweeping the lattice as repeating comb/hook textures, rainbow hue descending, with bright horizontal flash bands at the cyan and red hue crossings. Orig shows ~1.8 hue cycles in 12 s with thick saturated white flash bands; port shows ~2.4 cycles with thinner, less blown-out bands. Same structure, same 25% tempo gap.
feedback: Slow the whole animation by ~25%: the original's hue completes a full 0->360 revolution in 6.55 s and fires one pulse every 3.275 s; the port does 5.25 s and 2.62 s. One global rate constant scaled by 5.25/6.55 = 0.80 should line both up.

The pulse peak is roughly 3x too weak and never desaturates. At its climax the original drives EVERY pixel to full white (whole-rig mean 252 of 255, 225/256 pixels at >=250) for about one frame at 40 fps; the port's climax is a coloured wash at whole-rig mean ~79 with essentially no saturated pixels. The pulse envelope needs a much larger multiplier and needs to push the colour to white (all three channels railed), not just brighten the current hue.

The port splits each pulse into two flashes separated by a hard black notch (~0.2-0.3 s apart, 4-5 fully black frames between). The original fires a single flash per hue crossing. Something in the port's pulse envelope is being folded/rectified so it crosses zero twice per event — it should be one monotonic rise-and-fall.

The port goes fully black too often. The original blacks out only around its hue-0 pulse (once per 6.55 s hue cycle); the port blacks out roughly every 2.6 s, i.e. around every pulse. Once the doubled-flash and tempo issues are fixed, check that the hue-180 pulse rides on top of the normal band without ever dropping the whole rig to zero — on the original it does not (its hue-180 bell never dips below mean ~18).

Everything else already matches and should not be touched: the ~2-3 px band width and its ~250 peak, the band's slow rotation and sweep, the soft background gradient, the monotonic full-wheel hue walk and its direction, seed-independence and frame-rate independence.
